22 beliefs were wrong; 3 of them lived longer than a month

Each bar runs from when a claim was made to when a check withdrew it (label: what corrected it)

corrected within a month

lived over a month

9

Details

The long-lived ones share a pattern recorded in memory: a stale reduction or a self-consistency test that cannot see the error (the 29-June HV CSV, the y mirror, the ~1° "floor"). The rules that came out of them: date every reduction against the basis changes; pin every axis sign to an external fact; a check that reuses the suspect index proves nothing.

Details

Decisions of 2026-10-28: rebuild all calibration products in the DAG including the templates; bow block on all five chambers by the same recipe; LM fitter merged only if its fleet gate passes; trigger-track rule as a downstream selection.

Physics inputs, not calibrations: σ0 = 0.30 mm, Dp per chamber, det4 D_rc,y 2.2e-4 (beam), the timing-free gaps and the timing v per golden row (rerun/calib/physics_inputs.json). S4 re-measures them; if one moves beyond its error the calibration is redone for that chamber.

Realistic timing: engineering and the S1 submission tonight; G1 and the vrefit + pass submission tomorrow morning unless the engineering goes fast.

What this does not rule out

The history is as complete as the records: a lesson nobody wrote down is not here

• n_TOF-only lessons are listed only where they changed the detector model

• Lessons were dated by the commit or note that recorded them, not when first suspected

• "In the chain" means a default in the code on main today; the pass is the test

• Still running at publication: GD det4 spark row and the LM fleet gate

• Limits by design: det4 dead stripes, det7 X tails, the X asymmetry mechanism

• Never audited: bench degrador rings per run

• Physics inputs (σ0, Dp, gaps, timing v) are re-checked downstream, not refit

• Open checks before the archive: the 14 GA channels, ch 372, 10 rows without gas times
